results.inputs: a cylinder modelled to the printed description - 36 disks, each periphery divided into 26 parts, each disk carrying the letters in a different random ordering - and one 36-character plaintext block set along the reference bar
results.expected: the text says the 25 other parallel reference positions each define a ciphertext: the model must yield exactly 26 rows, the reference row reading back the block and the other 25 being distinct from it and from one another

observed.randomOrderings: generated from a fixed seed here; Figure 7.3 prints fragments of five wheel rows, not a complete ordering, so no historical order is claimed

results.inputs: the 127 whole 36-letter blocks of the sample read from row 17 of the cylinder, plus a permutation table built by probing the device once per wheel and per alphabet letter
results.expected: the handbook states a family of t permutations with the subscript taken modulo t (hac-ch7.txt:1098-1099). Tested against that statement: the permutation acting at position i must equal the one at i + 36 for all 4562 positions checked, the device must present exactly 36 distinct permutations rather than more or fewer, and the row read from the device must equal that family applied with the subscript modulo 36. The equality of position i with position i + 36 holds by construction for this model and is reported as a model property; what is measured is that exactly 36 distinct permutations appear, and the printed sentences are re-read from the registered text.

observed.permutationForm: ci = ei(mi) with the subscript i taken modulo t (t = 36)
observed.whatThisChecks: the count of distinct permutations (36) is measured over the model; the equality of position i with position i + 36 holds by construction because the model indexes the wheels that way, and is reported as a model property rather than as evidence about the source
